concepts.name: Wash them with water
concepts.why: Name vs passages: 'A bronze basin' is in Exod 30:18 only; Exod 29:4, Lev 8:6 and Lev 16:4 name no basin (the same ground on which Heb 10:22 was dropped in round 1). Rename in Exod 29:4's own words; all six passages then hold it and every note stays as it is.

Name vs passages: the name says 'make atonement'; Lev 1:5 has the priests present the blood and the verse does not mention atonement (that is in 1:4). Same ground on which Heb 8:3 was dropped in round 1. Five passages remain, which meets the minimum.

concepts.name: Those who serve at the altar partake of its offerings
concepts.why: Name vs passages: 'Those who serve at the altar' alone is the subject of concepts 1 and 4; what all six passages say is that they eat the offerings. Use the full words of 1 Cor 9:13, which every passage then holds. Notes unchanged.

concepts.name: The guilt of her priests
concepts.why: Name vs passages (new in round 2 after Jer 2:8, Isa 28:7 and Hos 6:9 were added): 'who despise My name' is Mal 1:6 only. The others say the priests profane, do violence, drink, teach for a price, murder, shed blood, or never asked 'Where is the LORD?'. Lam 4:13's 'the guilt of her priests' is the texts' own plain label for all eight. Secular scholar / Jewish reader: a name drawn from one prophet should not stand over seven others. No note changes.

Duplicate pair with 54: 'A kingdom of priests' and 'A royal priesthood' are one sub-theme, God's people called priests (1 Pet 2:9 is itself the words of Exod 19:6, 'a holy nation'). Receive 54's 1 Pet 2:5, 1 Pet 2:9 and Rev 20:6 here: seven passages, within the limit, and no 3-passage concept that needed a filler. Keep this name; all Revelation, Isaiah, Exodus and Peter notes stay as they are.

Merge into 53 (same sub-theme named twice). Separately, Rev 20:6 was moved here in round 1 only to reach the 3-passage minimum; it does not say 'royal' and its 'first resurrection ... a thousand years' puts the concept in the order-of-last-things dispute (Baptist/dispensational, amillennial, Reformed, Catholic and Orthodox readers differ on who is meant), which a filler placement under a name taken from 1 Pet 2:9 appears to settle. If the merge is refused, Rev 20:6 should leave this concept.

concepts.name: Sacrifices acceptable to God
note_fixes: Philippians 2:17: add here from concept 56 (note unchanged: 'even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith')
concepts.why: Name vs passages (new in round 2): 'a sacrifice of praise' is Heb 13:15 and, loosely, Ps 50:14 and Hos 14:2; Ps 51:17 (broken spirit), Rom 12:1 (bodies) and Phil 4:18 (gifts) are not praise. 'Sacrifices acceptable to God' is 1 Pet 2:5's words and Phil 4:18's 'acceptable sacrifice', and every passage holds it. Plain label, so it does not say the Old Testament verses are met by the New Testament ones. Ps 141:2 is already under 'To burn incense before the LORD'; dropping it here makes room for Phil 2:17 and keeps the limit of eight.

Phil 2:17 is Paul himself poured out on the Philippians' 'sacrifice and service of your faith'; it is not people presented to the LORD and fits 55. Five passages remain. Reader caution only, no change required: Isa 66:20 ('your brothers ... as a gift') beside Rom 15:16 (Gentiles as an offering) is the image shared, and the note keeps each in its own words; a Jewish or secular reader should not take the grouping to say Isaiah points to Romans, so the name must stay the plain label it is.

secondary_or_links: Duplicate pair (the one the brief asks for): concepts 53 'A kingdom of priests' and 54 'A royal priesthood' are the same sub-theme named twice. Merge as given in the concept entries. No other pair in the 58 is the same sub-theme: 15/16 (teaching), 41/49 (both hold Num 25:13), 42/45 (both hold 1 Sam 2:35), 13/57 and 35/36/37 each differ in what they say.

Link 'Law/Wisdom': the passages are law and instruction, none are Wisdom Literature. If 'Law/Wisdom' is not a published theme (the published themes now include 'The Law' and 'Wisdom Literature' separately), the link should be 'The Law'. The coordinator should confirm against the brief's fixed list; I cannot see that list.
Secondary concepts: accepted as drafted. Each node's notes are exact quotations and none says one testament is fulfilled in or points to the other.

Order, as nine readers would take it: accepted. Concepts 48-52 read as a run (Melchizedek, permanent, changed, great high priest, once for all) and a reader could take the run as a story that Aaron's priesthood ended. It stays safe only because every name is a quotation, Zadok (5), the Levitical covenant (41) and the priests' blessing (58, last) are kept in the Aaronic frame, and no name asserts succession. Do not rename any of 49-52 to a summarising phrase.

Concept 57 'Draw near to God' (not changed): Jer 30:21 and Num 16:5 are the Old Testament side of a concept that is mostly Hebrews. The names are the shared plain words 'bring near' and 'approach'; do not add a note that ties Jer 30:21's 'leader' to Heb 7:25.

Last concept: the priests' blessing (Num 6:24-26 and the blessing passages) is the theme's own words of hope, from within the theme, and the dark sub-themes (13, 42, 43, 39) are all present unsoftened. Accepted.
